advice.strongestCounterargument: Juancho's own simulation prefers Pickens - he is 78.3% to survive and 78.3% to be best available at 32, while the pair row shows Bowers and Pickens are both there in 55.7% of runs and bIfAGone says if Pickens goes first, Bowers still survives 86.2% of the time, implying we can often get both by taking Pickens now.
advice.whyRecommendationStillWins: That 86.2% is conditioned on Pickens being the one taken, which is exactly the branch where roster 10 spends a pick on a receiver instead of the tight end; the unconditional 74.3% is the honest number, and the WR replacement cost is trivial (a 16-man tier with Rice at 91.7%, Higgins 93.3%, McMillan 93%) against a 15.7-point TE cliff we cannot recover from.
advice.expectedNextPickPlan: At 32 take the best of Pickens (78.3%), Malik Nabers (81.7%), A.J.
